parallel.requirements: Recognized the pure Rust, zero dependency, black-box porting task; identified exact CLI/stoi semantics, hopscotch-map bucket/load-factor behavior, float formatting, Cargo layout, and required test11.rs entry.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent retained implementation ownership while delegating spec verification and adversarial review/fuzz workflows; children were verification aids rather than owners of final output.
parallel.implementation: Parent implemented cxx and tsl modules, test11.rs, Cargo metadata, formatting and stoi emulation, then fixed write-error behavior, edition-sensitive imports, overflow hardening, and stale tests.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent wrote the final project directly into /output, rebuilt /output/test11 and cargo release artifacts, and left a complete artifact tree accepted by the evaluator.
parallel.verification: Parent ran reference probes, count sweeps, CLI/error differentials, cargo tests, formatter corpus checks, warning builds, /dev/full checks, and independent expected-table comparisons.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The code artifact was correct by official evaluation, but both workflows were killed with null results and the parent produced no final response because it was still waiting.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same source, CLI, output formatting, black-box, pure Rust, zero dependency, Cargo, and /output/test11.rs requirements without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final communication end to end with workflows and delegation disabled.
serial.implementation: Created Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, tsl modules, cxx modules, and test11.rs; fixed warning and decimal-test issues during local iteration.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built /output/test11 and target/release/test11 in the package root structure and preserved the required source entry file.
serial.verification: Ran binary probes, 362-case and later 448-case differentials, byte-exact stdout checks, cargo builds/tests, and a 453929-value glibc formatter comparison.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished work is visible at closure; final response summarized verification and the official evaluator passed all 39 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required C++ behavior, CLI semantics, pure Rust/zero-dependency requirement, Cargo structure, and black-box restriction.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirement set and explicitly noted the same black-box and project-structure constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference affected the official outcome; both passed all official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split verification into background workflows but kept implementation and final artifact ownership in the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed all probing, coding, testing, and closure in a single trajectory with delegation disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added verifier/reviewer children that did not own deliverables; serial avoided child coordination and finished normally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow scripts gave children detailed context about the source, binary, known hypotheses, output paths, and non-editing review limits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used locally gathered context without handoffs and iterated within one context window.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material missing-context or interface-contract failure is evidenced; the main difference is that parallel children never returned aggregate results before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a richer port with cxx and tsl modules at package root paths, then refined it after differential failures and build checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a Cargo project under src plus package-root test11.rs, then fixed decimal and warning issues after tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on behavior accepted by the official evaluator; implementation organization differed but not task correctness.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched two workflows but never consumed a completed workflow result; it blocked on TaskOutput for the spec workflow near the end.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and wrote a normal final completion response after local checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's child-result lifecycle stayed open at termination, while serial had no join dependency and closed cleanly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent directly owned /output writes and integrated fixes itself; child writes were scratch/spec/review artifacts and did not overwrite the accepted deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all source files and build outputs itself in /output without concurrent workspace ownership.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision explains an outcome difference; parallel shared scratch state existed but the final /output artifact was parent-controlled and passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed strong local checks before the failed wait, including 1366 differentials, formatter corpus checks, cargo tests, and independent expected-table comparison.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed strong local checks too, including 362/448 differentials, formatter corpus checks, cargo builds/tests, and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had evaluator-aligned verification sufficient for the official pass; parallel attempted additional child review but did not need it for official correctness.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent additional time and tokens on two workflows and then blocked on a workflow result until returncode 143, leaving no final text.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in the time budget with returncode 0, no subagents, and a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The official outcomes are equal, but parallel had a coordination-specific closure failure while serial closed normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official solution outcome: both current completed cell/status.json evaluations passed all 39 testcases. The material task-solving difference is that serial completed and reported normally, while parallel produced a passing artifact but timed out during a blocking wait for unfinished workflow output.
parallel_contributors: Parent implementation and local verification produced an accepted artifact before timeout.
Background workflows remained unfinished and the parent blocked on TaskOutput near the deadline, preventing final response.
serial_contributors: Single-agent control completed probing, implementation, verification, and final response without delegation joins.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs fixed local implementation/test issues during development; none produced an official score difference.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern concerns parallel process closure rather than official solution pass/fail

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly owned and produced the implementation in /output before waiting on verifier workflows.
The parent integrated all implementation changes itself; no separately owned components required an unassigned reconciliation owner.
The parent assembled the Cargo project, root test11.rs, and executable artifacts before the timeout.
The parent owned the end-to-end implementation, build, test, and delivery pipeline; the failure was later closure while waiting.
Implementation was not blocked behind the spec workflow; the parent implemented and tested while the workflow ran.
The parent did not defer productive implementation until all investigations completed; coding and validation overlapped with workflow execution.
The indispensable implementation path was not starved; the parent completed and revalidated the artifact before the final wait.
Although there were many children and stalls, the directly evidenced failure is the parent's blind blocking wait on one workflow, not collective fan-out displacing unfinished required implementation.
Some child scopes were broad, but no single child owned indispensable final implementation whose unfinished work caused the official outcome or artifact to fail.
The executed child briefs contained the relevant task, binary, black-box, CLI, formatting, and build requirements; no omitted known requirement made child work unusable.
Children were verification/review agents, not separately assigned interoperating implementation components with missing interface contracts.
No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer and causing repeated work or wrong action.
No completed bulky handoff reached the parent and remained materially unconsumed; the workflows had null aggregate results.
No receiver consumed stale workflow output describing a superseded workspace and then performed invalid integration or verification.
No incompatible completed reports reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at an integration decision point.
The parent did not make a final unsupported whole-task completion decision; it had substantial integrated checks and then timed out while waiting.
The observed retries were workflow stall retries, but the pair does not show a retry lacking inherited state that caused repeated required implementation failure.

No child completed a delegated implementation that the parent failed to retrieve or adopt; implementation remained parent-owned.
No concrete verifier finding was completed and trapped below the parent; the workflow aggregate result was null because the parent waited into timeout.
The failed/killed children were verification auxiliaries, not required implementation owners whose unfinished scope the parent had to take over for a passing artifact.
No completed workflow result was available to the parent and ignored; the relevant workflows were still null/killed.

The parent had already completed and locally verified the artifact, then issued a blocking TaskOutput wait for an unfinished verifier workflow near the run deadline instead of inspecting progress non-blockingly or closing with the ready artifact.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel run was killed before producing any final response, even though the submitted artifact passed the official evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The absent verifier aggregate was not a completed concrete finding trapped below the parent; the actionable boundary was the blocking wait with no further monitoring or closure.

candidates.reason: No concurrent agents produced competing implementation designs in different files that required unresolved reconciliation.
Although workflow scratch files reused some paths, no same-source final implementation file collision was observed or required parent reconciliation.
There is no evidence that one actor replaced non-entry source owned by another in a way that invalidated implementation provenance.
The parent owned and rewrote /output/test11.rs itself; no concurrent child replaced the submitted entry source or executable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another actor's final-tree work and caused an unstable accepted artifact.
Shared scratch directories were used, but no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem affected the delivered solution.
No generated artifact from one concurrent actor was consumed as a false reference environment or contaminated the final verification result.

retained_patterns.reason: After completing and revalidating the port, the parent blocked on TaskOutput for an unfinished spec workflow instead of polling, harvesting partial progress, or closing with the ready artifact. The workflow state remained killed/result null and the process ended 143.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel run was killed before producing any final response, while the artifact still passed 39/39 official tests.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The issue is not a concrete completed verifier finding that failed to return; the workflow had null aggregate result and the parent chose a blocking wait.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Did not also retain Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Early Child Termination, Missing Verifier Return, No Failure Takeover, or Late Finalization for the same killed-workflow/timeout chain.
